model.name: Geometry / Coordinate Reference
model.purpose: Provide a format-neutral mixin that lets any host record carry a spatially unambiguous geometry together with the coordinate reference context, operation pins, comparability preconditions and reproducibility evidence needed to read, bind, correct, validate, transform, compare, export and retire that geometry without ambiguity.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-033 covers everything required to make a coordinate tuple interpretable and operable on a host record: the representation-neutral description of the geometry value, the coordinate reference context that gives it meaning (reference frame or datum ensemble, coordinate system and axes, units, and coordinate epoch for dynamic frames), the identifiers and registry release that bind that context to an authority, and the operation semantics that govern reading it as of an instant, binding it to a host, correcting it by supersession, validating it, transforming it under an externally executed pinned operation, deciding whether two geometries may be compared, exporting it into a lossy binding, and signalling readiness for tombstoning. The model calculates, validates and reports; it holds no storage layout, no interface contract and no execution engine. It is a mixin: it never asserts the identity, classification or lifecycle of the real-world thing whose location it describes, and it never re-issues definitions owned by a geodetic registry authority.
in_scope: Representation-neutral description of a geometry value: geometry kind, spatial and coordinate dimension, coordinate tuple ordering, edge interpretation, units and precision.

The coordinate reference context that makes coordinates interpretable: CRS reference and issuing authority, reference frame or datum ensemble, coordinate system axes and units, and coordinate epoch where the frame is dynamic.
As-of resolution rules that select which geometry version and which coordinate reference context version applied at a stated event instant and a stated observation instant.
Binding of a geometry and its coordinate reference context to a host record, including host reference, geometry role, cardinality and declared storage CRS.
Correction of geometry values or coordinate reference context by supersession, with originals held immutable and impacted references reported.
Validation of geometry structure and of coordinate reference context completeness, including conditional obligations for dynamic reference frames and area-of-validity checks.
Declaration and pinning of a coordinate operation together with engine, registry release and grid or deformation resources, for execution by an external system.
Comparability preconditions that must hold before two geometries are topologically related, measured or aggregated.
Export and redaction of a geometry into a target binding with explicit, itemised loss reporting.
Tombstone marking and disposition-readiness signalling, including hold indications, for retention executed elsewhere.
Provenance and reproducibility evidence for every derived coordinate value.
out_of_scope: Maintenance, curation or re-issue of authoritative CRS, reference frame and coordinate-operation definitions; those are owned by the registry authority.
Acquisition, hosting, licensing or redistribution of transformation grids and deformation models.
Execution of coordinate arithmetic; the numerical engine, its algorithms and its versions are external resources referenced by pin.
Persistence, storage layout, spatial indexing and query planning.
Authorization enforcement, credential handling and policy evaluation; this model carries only an authorization reference and records the external decision reference.
Capture, retention and immutability guarantees of audit trails for operations performed on the geometry.
Execution of retention schedules, disposition approval, legal-hold administration and physical destruction of records.
Cartographic rendering, symbolisation, generalisation for display and map production.
Gazetteer, postal addressing and administrative-boundary authority.
Network topology, routing, and coverage or raster grid processing semantics.
Sensor observation, survey campaign and instrument calibration semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Authoritative geodetic registry (EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset and equivalent national registries)
boundary_notes.distinction: This model references a CRS, reference frame or coordinate-operation code together with its issuing authority, the registry release in force and the record status (valid, superseded, deprecated). It never defines, curates, corrects or re-issues those definitions, and it does not mirror registry content as local truth.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Coordinate transformation engine and geodetic software
boundary_notes.distinction: This model states which operation, resources, epochs and tolerances must be used and what evidence must be returned. Candidate discovery heuristics, numerics, pipeline construction, performance and engine defaults belong to the engine; the model consumes the engine's identity and version as a pin.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Serialization and interface bindings (WKT/WKB, GeoJSON, GML, GeoParquet, database and HTTP API bindings)
boundary_notes.distinction: Bindings are projections of the same semantics. The model records which binding was used and what that binding could not carry; it never elevates one binding to canonical status and never inherits a binding's fixed defaults as model-wide semantics.

This model emits derivation assertions shaped as entity, activity, agent, used, wasGeneratedBy and wasDerivedFrom about coordinate values it reports. Storage, immutability, retention and the audit trail lifecycle of those assertions are owned by the provenance and audit model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Records retention, legal hold and disposition model
boundary_notes.distinction: This model reports disposition readiness and any asserted hold reference and can mark a tombstone. Schedules, approval, execution of destruction and the legal effect of a hold are owned by the retention model; invalidation is asserted, not performed.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Host feature or subject record model
boundary_notes.distinction: A spatial thing is disjoint from its geometry: the host owns the identity, classification and lifecycle of the thing, and may carry several geometries of differing accuracy or time. This mixin owns only the geometry and its coordinate reference context.

Plate-fixed frame definitions, geopotential datums, intra-frame velocity models and their rollout timelines are set by the national authority. This model consumes them as referenced, versioned external resources and records the resulting re-derivation obligation.

sources.title: OGC Abstract Specification Topic 2: Referencing by coordinates Corrigendum
sources.version_or_date: Version 5.0.1, 2021-07-02 (OGC 18-005r5; identical to ISO 19111:2019 with Amendment 1)
sources.relevance: Normative abstract model for coordinate reference systems, reference frames, datum ensembles, coordinate systems and axes, coordinate operations, dynamic CRS, coordinate epoch, point motion operations and compound CRS. Primary basis for what a coordinate reference context must contain.

sources.title: OGC API - Features - Part 2: Coordinate Reference Systems by Reference corrigendum
sources.relevance: Normative treatment of CRS by reference over an interface: supported CRS lists, storage CRS declaration, storageCrsCoordinateEpoch for dynamic CRS, CRS assertion on responses, and explicit failure for unsupported CRS. Evidence that CRS context must be declared and negotiated rather than assumed.

sources.title: WKT Coordinate Reference Systems - OGC Standard Representation (Geographic information - Well-known text representation of coordinate reference systems)
sources.relevance: Defines the structure and content of well-known text for CRS and for coordinate operations, aligned to ISO 19111:2019 with Amendments 1 and 2. Basis for treating WKT as one lossy projection with a defined expressive range, and for the deprecation of WKT version 1.

sources.title: RFC 7946: The GeoJSON Format
sources.relevance: Fixes a single geographic CRS with longitude-latitude ordering, removes the prior crs member because alternative CRS caused interoperability failures, and excludes topology, curved geometries and alternative CRS. Primary evidence of concrete, bounded projection loss on export.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Requires every timestamp to carry a stated relationship to UTC via Z or a numeric offset, defines the seconds field including leap-second values, and defines -00:00 as unknown local offset. Basis for the timestamp rule and for separating record time from geodetic coordinate epoch.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies the entity, activity, agent, used, wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasRevisionOf, Plan and qualified-association vocabulary used to shape transformation evidence, supersession and invalidation assertions without owning audit storage.

sources.title: Computation of coordinate operations between two CRS - PROJ documentation
sources.relevance: Documents that candidate operations are discovered from registry tables and ranked by twelve criteria including local grid availability, known accuracy and area of use, that missing grids change the outcome, that ballpark operations may be substituted, and that a user may pin an operation by code, pipeline or pivot CRS. Primary evidence that transformation results are non-deterministic unless pinned.

sources.title: OGC Testbed-18: Reference Frame Transformation Engineering Report
sources.relevance: Identifies gaps in frame-equivalency determination (reliance on datum name or identifier), the restriction of dynamic datums to geodetic and vertical frames, and the comparative expressiveness of GML versus WKT for encoding coordinate operations. Source for known limits and for non-terrestrial and engineering gaps.

sources.title: Geodesy - EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset
sources.organization: International Association of Oil and Gas Producers (IOGP), Geomatics Committee
sources.version_or_date: Accessed 2026-09-04; dataset registry at epsg.org, data model aligned to ISO 19111:2019 since the October 2020 platform migration
sources.relevance: Authority statement for the EPSG Dataset: maintained by IOGP members through the Geodesy Subcommittee, distributed publicly subject to acceptance of Terms of Use, with a data model covering dynamic datums, geoid-based vertical datums, datum ensembles and derived projected CRS. Basis for registry references, release pinning and licensing holds.

sources.title: OGC API - Features - Part 1: Core Corrigendum
sources.relevance: Establishes an interface-scoped default CRS with longitude-first axis order and identifies it by OGC definition http URI, and defines four- and six-value bounding boxes. Evidence that defaults are binding-scoped, not model-wide, and that axis order must be declared explicitly.

sources.title: Spatial Data on the Web Best Practices
sources.organization: World Wide Web Consortium and Open Geospatial Consortium
sources.relevance: States that spatial things are disjoint from geometries and that one thing may have several geometries at different accuracies or times, that coordinate reference systems must be chosen to suit the application, that how coordinate values are encoded must be stated, and that geometries should be requestable and returnable in a specific CRS. Basis for the mixin boundary and for the export negotiation surface.

sources.title: GeoParquet Specification 1.1.0
sources.organization: GeoParquet / Open Geospatial Consortium community standard
sources.relevance: Carries CRS as PROJJSON, distinguishes an absent crs field (implying a default) from an explicit null crs (undefined CRS), carries coordinate epoch as a decimal year at column rather than geometry granularity, and distinguishes planar from spherical edge interpretation. Concrete evidence of binding-specific loss and of edge semantics affecting comparability.

sources.title: OGC GeoSPARQL - A Geographic Query Language for RDF Data
sources.relevance: Defines multiple geometry serializations with differing CRS-carrying rules, three topological relation families (Simple Features, Egenhofer, RCC8), and treats the influence of reference systems and units of measurement on geometric computation as a first-class concern. Basis for the comparability gate and for serialization-specific CRS defaults.

sources.title: New Datums / NSRS Modernization
sources.relevance: Documents replacement of an existing horizontal datum misaligned by roughly 2.2 metres and a vertical datum biased and tilted at the metre level, by four plate-fixed terrestrial reference frames and a geopotential datum. Primary evidence that reference-frame change forces re-derivation and that regional assumptions must be recorded, not embedded.

sources.title: OGC Naming Authority - Procedures
sources.relevance: Defines how persistent identifiers for OGC resources, including definitions such as CRS, are assigned as http URIs under a governed namespace and as URNs, and how external authorities are registered. Basis for the governed-global-identifier tier of the identity priority and for namespace guidance.

sources.title: OGC Simple Features Access - Part 1: Common Architecture
sources.relevance: Defines the simple feature geometry class hierarchy (Point, Curve, Surface, GeometryCollection) and states that each geometric object is associated with a spatial reference system describing the coordinate space in which it is defined. Basis for geometry-kind classification and for the geometry-to-SRS association requirement.

bundles.name: Coordinate Context Operation Lifecycle
bundles.description: Operations that resolve, bind, correct and retire a geometry together with its coordinate reference context on a host record, expressed without reference to any storage engine or interface protocol.
bundles.rationale: The abstract referencing model makes a coordinate meaningless without its coordinate reference system, and ambiguous without a coordinate epoch where the frame is dynamic. Any read, binding or correction that does not carry the exact context version in force therefore produces an uninterpretable value, so context resolution and versioning are lifecycle concerns rather than presentation concerns.

layers.name: Resolution and Host Binding
layers.description: How a caller determines which geometry and coordinate reference context apply at a stated instant, how that context is attached to a host record, and which preconditions a request must satisfy before any mutation is proposed.

findings.name: As-of resolution of geometry and coordinate reference context
findings.description: Determines which geometry version and which coordinate reference context version apply for a stated instant, which registry release and coordinate epoch qualify the returned coordinates, and what must be returned when no context is in force. Resolution never falls back to an implied default coordinate reference system.

answer_data: Event instant as an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and explicit offset or Z
Observation or ingestion instant in the same form
Identifier of the context version selected by that instant
Selector precedence rule applied when both are supplied

answer_data: Dynamic or static frame indicator
Coordinate epoch as a decimal year
Frame reference epoch of the datum
Statement that coordinates are ambiguous where the frame is dynamic and the epoch is absent

questions.text: Which registry release was in force for the resolved context, and what was the status of the referenced code at that release?
answer_data: Registry authority identifier
Registry release version and its release date
Record status: valid, superseded or deprecated
Superseding record reference where one exists

questions.text: Which authorization reference accompanied the read, and which external decision reference was returned for it?
answer_data: Authorization reference identifier presented by the caller
External policy decision reference and outcome indicator
Scope of the subject and resource the decision covered
Indicator of whether a precision-reduced view was served

Nearest earlier and nearest later context version references
Assertion that no default coordinate reference system was substituted
Diagnostic reason text

data_elements.name: As-of instant
data_elements.description: The instant against which the applicable geometry and coordinate reference context version are selected, qualified by which time axis it denotes.

data_elements.name: Resolved context version reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the exact geometry and coordinate reference context version that the resolution returned.

data_elements.name: Coordinate epoch
data_elements.description: The reference time, expressed as a decimal year, to which coordinates in a dynamic reference frame are referred. It is a geodetic quantity and is never used as a record timestamp.

data_elements.name: Registry release reference
data_elements.description: Authority and release version of the geodetic registry that was in force when the context was resolved, together with the status of the referenced code at that release.

data_elements.name: Resolution outcome code
data_elements.description: Coded result of the as-of resolution distinguishing resolved, ambiguous, not-in-force and unresolvable-reference outcomes.

artifacts.name: Resolved coordinate context snapshot
artifacts.description: A reported, non-authoritative snapshot of exactly what a caller was given for a stated as-of instant: geometry version reference, coordinate reference context, coordinate epoch, registry release and outcome code. It is evidence of what was resolved, not a second copy of the record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the host system's own snapshot record key where one is issued; otherwise a Dimension-assigned ULID. The snapshot always carries, but is never identified by, the as-of instant.

findings.name: Binding a geometry and coordinate reference context to a host record
findings.description: Establishes the attachment between a host record and a geometry with its coordinate reference context: which identifier binds them, what role the geometry plays for the host, how many such geometries may coexist, which reference frame kind is bound, and which storage coordinate reference system is declared.

questions.text: Which identifier binds this geometry and coordinate reference context to its host, and which authority issued that identifier?
answer_data: Binding identifier and its issuing authority
Host record reference and the host model that owns it
Identifier tier used: master-system key, governed global identifier or Dimension-assigned identifier

questions.text: What role does this geometry play for the host, and how many geometries of that role may coexist?
answer_data: Geometry role code, for example extent, representative point, service area or centroid
Cardinality permitted for that role
Rule for selecting a primary geometry where several exist at differing accuracy or time

questions.text: Which kind of coordinate reference system is bound, and is its datum a single realization or an ensemble?
answer_data: CRS kind: geodetic, projected, vertical, compound, engineering, parametric or temporal
Reference frame or datum ensemble reference
Ensemble indicator and the stated ensemble accuracy where applicable
Coordinate system axes with their units and declared order

questions.text: Which coordinate reference system is declared as the storage CRS for this binding, and which others may it be served in?
answer_data: Storage CRS reference and its coordinate epoch where the frame is dynamic
List of CRS references the binding may be served in
Statement that any served CRS other than storage requires a pinned transformation

data_elements.name: Binding identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier for the attachment of a geometry and coordinate reference context to a host record.

data_elements.name: Host record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the record whose spatial location this mixin describes; the host owns the identity and lifecycle of the thing itself.

data_elements.name: Geometry role
data_elements.description: Coded role the geometry plays for the host, distinguishing several coexisting geometries of the same host.

data_elements.name: Coordinate reference system reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the CRS definition as authority, code and registry release, or as a governed definition URI.

data_elements.name: Coordinate reference system kind
data_elements.description: Classification of the bound CRS as geodetic, projected, vertical, compound, engineering, parametric or temporal.

data_elements.name: Datum ensemble indicator
data_elements.description: Indicates that the referenced datum is an ensemble of realizations rather than a single realization, with the ensemble accuracy that bounds its internal ambiguity.

data_elements.name: Declared storage CRS
data_elements.description: The CRS in which the bound coordinates are held, distinguished from any CRS in which they may be served.

artifacts.name: Geometry and coordinate reference binding record
artifacts.description: The reported binding proposal or current binding state: host reference, geometry role, geometry value, coordinate reference context, storage CRS and permitted served CRS. Committing it to storage is performed by an external system.
media_or_form: tabular column set with attached metadata
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the host system's authoritative binding key where the host system of record issues one; otherwise by a governed definition URI where the binding is itself published; otherwise by a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID.

findings.name: Operation preconditions, idempotency and explicit failure
findings.description: The precondition envelope that every geometry or coordinate reference operation carries: the idempotency key that makes a repeated request safe, the version precondition that rejects a stale write, the authorization reference resolved by an external decision point, and the failure vocabulary that forbids silent defaulting.

questions.text: Which idempotency key scopes a repeated create or correction request, and over what window must the same key yield the same reported outcome?
answer_data: Idempotency key value and the scope it is unique within
Replay window duration
Outcome equivalence rule for a replayed key
Behaviour when the same key arrives with a different payload

questions.text: Which version precondition must a mutating request carry so that a stale write is rejected rather than merged?
answer_data: Expected version token of the current binding
Comparison rule and rejection outcome on mismatch
Statement that no automatic merge of geometry or CRS context is performed

questions.text: Which authorization reference and policy reference must accompany the request, and which external point returns the decision?
answer_data: Authorization reference identifier
Policy reference identifier
External decision point reference and returned decision reference
Statement that this model performs no evaluation or enforcement

questions.text: Which distinct failure codes are emitted for an unresolvable CRS, a missing coordinate epoch, an unavailable transformation resource, a precondition mismatch and a hold conflict?
answer_data: Enumerated failure codes with their triggering condition
Retryable or terminal classification for each code
Required diagnostic references, such as the missing resource or blocking hold reference
Prohibition on substituting a default CRS, epoch or ballpark result in place of a failure

data_elements.name: Idempotency key
data_elements.description: Caller-supplied key that makes a repeated create or correction request produce the same reported outcome within a declared window.

data_elements.name: Expected version token
data_elements.description: Optimistic concurrency precondition naming the binding version the caller believes is current; a mismatch is a terminal rejection.

data_elements.name: Authorization reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the authorization grant presented with the request. It is carried, never evaluated, by this model.

data_elements.name: External policy decision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the decision returned by the external enforcement point, retained so that a report can be correlated by the audit owner.

data_elements.name: Operation failure code
data_elements.description: Coded, enumerated failure outcome that names the unsatisfied precondition or unresolvable reference.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These elements are request-scoped parameters and returned outcome codes on a single operation call. They have no independent existence, no addressable state and no consumer beyond the call that carried them, so issuing an artifact for them would create a second, competing record of an operation. The durable trace of a request belongs to the external audit and provenance record model, which owns capture, correlation and retention of decision and idempotency references; reproducing it here would claim audit-trail ownership that this model explicitly does not hold. The context is therefore purely inline reference data attached to the operation envelope.

layers.name: Correction by Supersession and Closure
layers.description: How a geometry or coordinate reference context is corrected without mutating an original, and how a binding is marked for closure with disposition readiness reported to the party that owns retention.

findings.name: Correction by supersession over immutable originals
findings.description: Governs how a geometry value or a coordinate reference context is corrected: originals remain immutable, every correction is a new version that names what it supersedes and why, and every host reference or derived geometry affected by the correction is reported so referential integrity can be restored by their owners.

questions.text: Which states may a geometry and coordinate reference context version occupy between issue and supersession?
answer_data: Enumerated version states, for example proposed, in force, superseded and invalidated
Permitted state transitions and the trigger for each
Instant of each transition as an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and explicit offset or Z
Rule that a superseded version remains readable and is never edited in place

questions.text: Which prior version does this correction supersede, and what reason and evidence justify it?
answer_data: Reference to the superseded version
Correction reason code, for example measurement error, wrong CRS assignment, registry deprecation or reference-frame change
Reference to the evidence that supports the correction
Responsible agent reference for the correction

questions.text: Which host references and derived geometries must be re-pointed or re-derived once this version is superseded?
answer_data: List of incoming references to the superseded version
List of derived geometries produced from it and their evidence record references
Re-derivation obligation indicator per dependent
Statement that re-pointing is executed by the owner of each dependent, not by this model

questions.text: Which classes of change require a new version rather than an annotation on the existing one?
answer_data: Change classes that force a new version, such as any coordinate value change, CRS reference change, epoch change or axis-order correction
Change classes recordable as annotation, such as descriptive remarks
Tolerance below which a coordinate change is still treated as a new version
Rationale for each threshold

data_elements.name: Context version identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one immutable version of a geometry and coordinate reference context binding.

data_elements.name: Superseded version reference
data_elements.description: Reference from a correction to the immediately prior version it replaces, forming an ordered supersession chain.

data_elements.name: Correction reason code
data_elements.description: Coded justification for issuing a new version, distinguishing data error from authority-driven change such as registry deprecation or reference-frame replacement.

data_elements.name: Effective interval
data_elements.description: The interval during which a version is in force, bounded by instants recorded with seconds and an explicit offset, and kept distinct from any coordinate epoch.

data_elements.name: Impacted reference set
data_elements.description: The reported set of incoming references and derived geometries affected by a supersession, with a re-derivation obligation flag per entry.

artifacts.name: Supersession and correction record
artifacts.description: The issued record of one correction: new version reference, superseded version reference, reason code, responsible agent, effective interval and the impacted reference set. It is shaped as a derivation and revision assertion so that downstream owners can act on it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the master system's own correction record key where the system of record issues one; otherwise by a Dimension-assigned ULID. The correction instant is recorded as an attribute and is never used as the identifier.

findings.name: Tombstone marking and disposition readiness
findings.description: Marks a binding as invalidated and reports whether it is ready for disposition: which retention policy governs it, whether a hold is asserted, which incoming references would break, and what minimal residual payload may survive. Execution of destruction is never performed here.

questions.text: Which retention rule governs disposition of this binding, and where is the governing policy defined?
answer_data: Retention policy reference and the model or authority that owns it
Minimum retention period and its start trigger
Statement that this model reports readiness only and executes no destruction

questions.text: Is a legal or regulatory hold asserted against this binding, and by which reference?
answer_data: Hold asserted indicator
Hold reference identifier and asserting authority
Hold assertion instant with seconds and explicit offset or Z
Rule that disposition readiness is false while any hold is unresolved

questions.text: Which incoming references would break on destruction, and what minimal residual payload must survive as a tombstone?
answer_data: List of incoming required and optional references
Residual payload profile: binding identifier, invalidation instant and superseded-by reference
Rule that no coordinate values are retained in the residual payload unless the retention owner directs otherwise
Blocking reference list returned when integrity would be violated

questions.text: Which coordinate precision or locational attributes must be removed or generalised before any residual record is kept?
answer_data: Location sensitivity classification of the binding
Generalisation or precision-reduction rule applied to any residual
Reference to the jurisdiction-specific rule that set the threshold
Indicator that generalisation was applied and by which reference

data_elements.name: Tombstone identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the marker that records a binding as invalidated while preserving referential resolvability.

data_elements.name: Invalidation instant
data_elements.description: The instant at which the binding was asserted to be no longer valid, recorded with seconds and an explicit offset or Z and distinguished from any later physical destruction performed elsewhere.

data_elements.name: Hold reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an asserted legal or regulatory hold that blocks disposition readiness.

data_elements.name: Retention policy reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally owned retention rule that governs disposition of this binding.

data_elements.name: Residual payload profile
data_elements.description: Declares which fields survive in the tombstone and which are removed or generalised, including any locational precision reduction.

artifacts.name: Binding tombstone marker
artifacts.description: The issued marker asserting that a binding is invalidated, carrying only the residual payload profile, the invalidation instant, any superseded-by reference and the disposition-readiness determination with blocking holds and references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Reuses the authoritative binding identifier issued by the host system of record so that dangling references still resolve; where no such identifier exists, a Dimension-assigned UUID is used. The invalidation instant is an attribute, never an identifier.

bundles.name: Geometry Computation, Comparison and Export
bundles.description: Operations that check, derive, relate and project geometry values: validating structure and coordinate reference context, pinning a transformation for external execution with reproducible evidence, gating comparison on compatible spatial semantics, and reporting loss on export into any binding.
bundles.rationale: Operation selection between two coordinate reference systems is heuristic and depends on registry content, locally available grids, area of use and engine version, so an unpinned transformation is not reproducible. Serializations each fix different defaults and each drop different parts of the context. Both facts make explicit pinning, explicit comparability preconditions and itemised loss reporting mandatory rather than advisory.

layers.name: Validation and Pinned Transformation
layers.description: How a geometry and its coordinate reference context are checked for completeness and structural admissibility, and how a coordinate transformation is specified so that an external engine can execute it and return re-derivable evidence.

findings.name: Validation of geometry structure and coordinate reference context completeness
findings.description: Defines the checks that must pass before a geometry is published or used: structural admissibility for the declared geometry kind, mandatory and conditionally mandatory coordinate reference context fields, agreement between declared axes, units and coordinate tuples, and containment within the area of validity of the referenced CRS and operation.

questions.text: Which structural conditions must a geometry satisfy for its declared geometry kind, and which failures are non-recoverable?
answer_data: Geometry kind from the simple feature hierarchy or an explicitly declared extension
Structural checks such as ring closure, ring orientation, self-intersection, minimum vertex count and nesting of interior rings
Per-check outcome with severity
Non-recoverable failure list that blocks publication

questions.text: Which coordinate reference context fields are mandatory before publication, and which become mandatory only for a dynamic reference frame?
answer_data: Unconditionally mandatory fields: CRS reference, issuing authority and coordinate dimension
Conditionally mandatory fields: coordinate epoch where the frame is dynamic, ensemble accuracy where the datum is an ensemble
Distinction between an absent CRS field and an explicitly undefined CRS value
Outcome when a mandatory field is missing

questions.text: Do the declared axis units, axis order and coordinate dimension agree with the actual coordinate tuples?
answer_data: Declared axis list with unit of measure and abbreviation per axis
Declared axis order and the order actually present in the tuples
Declared coordinate dimension versus observed tuple length
Mismatch outcome and the axis at which it was detected

questions.text: Does the geometry fall within the stated area of validity of the referenced CRS and of any pinned operation?
answer_data: Area of validity of the referenced CRS
Area of use of any pinned coordinate operation
Containment outcome, including partial containment
Severity assigned to out-of-extent coordinates

questions.text: Which validation severities are distinguished, and which of them block publication rather than warn?
answer_data: Severity vocabulary, for example blocking, warning and informational
Mapping of each check to a severity
Rule for aggregating severities into an overall outcome
Statement of who may waive a warning and under which reference

data_elements.name: Geometry kind
data_elements.description: Classification of the geometry value within the simple feature hierarchy or an explicitly declared extension beyond it.

data_elements.name: Coordinate dimension
data_elements.description: Number of ordinates in each coordinate tuple, distinguished from the topological dimension of the geometry.

data_elements.name: Axis declaration
data_elements.description: Ordered list of coordinate system axes with name, abbreviation, direction and unit of measure, establishing the authoritative tuple order for the bound CRS.

data_elements.name: Validation outcome
data_elements.description: Aggregate result of the validation run with per-check outcomes and severities.

data_elements.name: Area-of-validity check result
data_elements.description: Result of testing the geometry against the area of validity of the referenced CRS and the area of use of any pinned operation.

artifacts.name: Geometry and context validation report
artifacts.description: The issued report listing every check performed, its outcome, severity and the exact location or field at which it failed, together with the aggregate publication decision input. It reports; it does not gate publication itself.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the master system's validation run key where one is issued; otherwise a Dimension-assigned ULID, with the binding identifier and version carried as attributes. No date component is used as the identifier.

findings.name: Externally executed transformation under a pinned operation with reproducibility evidence
findings.description: Specifies a coordinate transformation as an explicit pin set rather than a request to convert: which operation, which engine and version, which registry release, which grid or deformation resources with checksums, which source and target epochs, and what accuracy is claimed. Execution belongs to an external engine; this finding governs what must be declared beforehand and what evidence must return.

questions.text: Which coordinate operation is pinned for this transformation, and which candidate operations were considered and rejected?

data_elements.name: Pinned operation reference

data_elements.name: Engine reference and version

data_elements.name: Transformation resource pin set

artifacts.name: Coordinate operation pin set

layers.name: Comparison Preconditions and Export Loss
layers.description: How two geometries are judged comparable before any spatial relation or measurement is admitted, and how a geometry is projected into a target binding with every loss itemised.

findings.name: Compatibility preconditions for comparing or relating geometries
findings.description: States the preconditions that must hold before a topological relation, distance, area or aggregation between two geometries is admissible: a common resolvable coordinate reference context, a compatible edge interpretation, an agreed epoch basis, and a relation family whose assumptions the geometries satisfy. Failure is reported, not silently repaired.

questions.text: Which conditions must hold before a topological or metric relation between two geometries is admitted?

Common CRS reference, or a pinned transformation reference that establishes one
Agreement of coordinate dimension and unit of measure

questions.text: Are the edges of the two geometries interpreted as planar or spherical, and does the chosen relation family assume one of these?

Relation family selected: Simple Features, Egenhofer or region connection calculus
Assumption of the selected family regarding edge interpretation
Outcome when the two operands declare different edge interpretations

questions.text: When the two operands carry different coordinate epochs, at which epoch is the comparison performed?

Selected comparison epoch and the rule that chose it
Reference to the point motion or transformation pin that aligned the operands
Outcome when one operand has no epoch and its frame is dynamic

questions.text: Does equality of the two CRS references actually establish equality of realization, or is one of them a datum ensemble?

Stated ensemble accuracy that bounds internal ambiguity
Rule that ensemble membership does not establish comparability below the ensemble accuracy
Precision threshold above which the comparison is admitted

questions.text: What is reported when comparability fails, and may a result ever be returned with a qualification instead?

Conditions under which a qualified result may be returned with the transformation and residual uncertainty stated
Prohibition on silently transforming an operand to force a comparison
Reference to the evidence record for any transformation that was applied

data_elements.name: Comparability outcome
data_elements.description: Coded determination of whether two geometries may be related, may be related only after a named transformation, or may not be related.

data_elements.name: Common coordinate reference basis
data_elements.description: The CRS in which the comparison is to be performed, together with the transformation pin reference for any operand that had to be brought to it.

data_elements.name: Edge interpretation
data_elements.description: Declares whether the segments between coordinate tuples are interpreted as planar straight lines or as geodesics on the spheroid of the CRS.

data_elements.name: Epoch alignment basis
data_elements.description: The coordinate epoch at which the comparison is performed and the rule or operation that aligned differing operand epochs to it.

data_elements.name: Relation family
data_elements.description: The topological relation vocabulary applied to the comparison and the semantic assumptions it carries.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Comparability is a precondition evaluated per comparison against the two operands as they stand at that moment; it has no independent subject and becomes stale the instant either operand is superseded. Issuing an artifact would create a durable assertion about a transient pairwise judgement and would compete with the transformation evidence record, which already carries the authoritative statement of any alignment that was actually performed. The determination is therefore expressed as inline predicate outcomes and failure codes returned with the comparison request, referencing the evidence record where a transformation was involved.

findings.name: Export and redaction into a target binding with loss reporting
findings.description: Governs projection of a geometry and its coordinate reference context into a target serialization, database or interface binding. Each binding carries a different subset of the semantics, so the export declares the target, itemises every loss with its magnitude, records any redaction applied, and identifies loss classes that must block the export outright.

questions.text: Which target binding is requested, and which parts of the coordinate reference context can that binding not carry?

Context fields the binding cannot express, such as coordinate epoch, ensemble accuracy or per-geometry CRS
Binding-fixed defaults that will override declared values, such as a mandated single CRS and axis order
Declared CRS actually written into the export

questions.text: Which specific losses occurred on this export, and what is the magnitude of each?
answer_data: Itemised loss list by class: CRS collapse, epoch loss, dimension loss, precision truncation, curve linearisation, topology loss, measure or ordinate loss, antimeridian splitting
Magnitude per item with unit, for example maximum displacement introduced by linearisation or truncation
Reversibility indicator per item
Count of features or vertices affected

questions.text: Which redaction or coordinate generalisation was applied before export, and under which reference?

Reference to the policy or decision that required it
Resulting effective precision or generalisation radius
Indicator that the export is generalised, carried in the export itself

questions.text: Which loss classes must block an export rather than merely be reported?
answer_data: Blocking loss classes and their thresholds
Rationale tying each threshold to a stated fitness-for-use
Override reference required to proceed despite a blocking loss
Failure code emitted when a blocking loss is detected

data_elements.name: Loss item list
