composition.target: WM-XCT-010 (registered parent model for spatial and geometric context)
composition.purpose: Places this mixin under its registered parent, which owns the broader spatial context container and the navigation placement. The parent does not redefine coordinate reference semantics; this model supplies them and only them.

composition.target: Host feature or subject record model adopting the mixin
composition.purpose: Attaches geometry and coordinate reference context to a host record. A spatial thing is disjoint from its geometry and may carry several geometries of differing accuracy or time, so identity, classification and lifecycle of the thing remain entirely with the host.

composition.target: Authoritative geodetic registry model (EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset and equivalent national registries)
composition.purpose: Carries the CRS, reference frame and coordinate-operation code, its issuing authority, the registry release in force and the record status. Registry curation, correction, deprecation decisions and terms-of-use administration remain with the registry authority.

composition.target: Coordinate transformation execution service model (geodetic engine and resource catalogue)
composition.purpose: Carries the pinned operation, engine identity and version, and resource digests, and validates the evidence returned. Candidate discovery heuristics, numerics, resource acquisition and execution belong wholly to the engine. Required only where a derived coordinate value is produced.

Shapes derivation, revision and invalidation assertions using entity, activity, agent, used, wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom and wasRevisionOf so that evidence is portable. Storage, immutability, correlation and retention of the provenance and audit trail are owned by that model; alignment is asserted, conformance is not claimed.

composition.target: Records retention, legal hold and disposition model
composition.purpose: Carries the retention policy reference and any asserted hold reference, and consumes them to report disposition readiness. Retention schedules, hold administration, disposition approval and physical destruction are executed entirely by that model.

Carries the authorization reference presented with a request and the decision reference returned. Policy authoring, evaluation and enforcement are performed by that model; this model neither evaluates nor enforces and holds no policy state.

composition.target: Temporal reference model (instants, intervals and calendars)
composition.purpose: Supplies the semantics of instants and intervals used for event time, observation time and effective intervals, recorded as RFC 3339 date-times. Coordinate epoch remains local to this model because it is a geodetic reference time, not a calendar instant.

composition.target: Unit of measure and quantity model
composition.purpose: Supplies units for coordinate system axes, accuracy values, tolerances and generalisation radii. Unit definitions, conversion factors and dimensional analysis belong to that model; this model carries unit references on axes and quantities.

composition.target: Serialization and interface binding profiles (WKT/WKB, GeoJSON, GML, GeoParquet, database and API bindings)
composition.purpose: Aligns the model's semantics with each binding's expressive range and records what each binding cannot carry. No binding is canonical, and a binding's fixed defaults are recorded as losses on export rather than adopted as model semantics.

composition.target: National geodetic authority reference-frame and deformation-model resources
composition.purpose: Carries references to plate-fixed frames, geopotential datums and velocity or deformation models as versioned external resources, and records the re-derivation obligation their replacement creates. Frame definition, publication and rollout timing belong to the national authority.

composition.target: Spatial relation and topological query model
composition.purpose: Specialises only the coordinate-reference precondition on spatial relations: which relation family may be applied, under which common reference basis, edge interpretation and epoch alignment. The relation vocabularies, their algebra and their evaluation remain defined and executed by that model.

owner_package_requirements: Name one accountable owner and one deputy for the adopted geometry and coordinate reference package. The owner approves the CRS allow-list, the pinned registry release, the default coordinate epoch policy and the blocking loss classes for export.

Declare the geodetic registry authority the Dimension adopts, the exact registry release pinned for operation lookup, the review cadence for new releases, and the procedure for handling codes that become superseded or deprecated between releases.
Declare, for every host collection that adopts the mixin, the storage CRS, the CRS values it may be served in, whether the frame is dynamic, and the coordinate epoch policy that applies.

Name the external systems that own persistence, authorization enforcement, audit retention, transformation execution, grid and deformation resource acquisition, and physical destruction, with escalation references for each.
Record the licensing position for every registry, grid and deformation resource the Dimension relies on, including redistribution restrictions, before those resources appear in any pin set.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use the issuing authority's own namespace for every CRS, reference frame and coordinate-operation reference, expressed either as a governed definition URI or as an authority and code pair together with the registry release. Never re-mint a local code for a registered definition and never alias one authority's code into another authority's namespace. Reserve the Dimension namespace strictly for locally created identifiers: binding identifiers, context version identifiers, pin set identifiers and report identifiers. Keep the Dimension namespace disjoint from every authority namespace so that a reference can always be traced to its issuer.
registry_links: EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset, maintained by the IOGP Geodesy Subcommittee, for CRS, reference frame, datum ensemble and coordinate-operation codes: https://www.iogp.org/workstreams/engineering/geomatics/geodesy/
OGC Naming Authority procedures for governed persistent identifiers and http URIs used for OGC-issued definitions: https://docs.ogc.org/pol/09-046r6.html
PROJ operation computation documentation, used as the reference for engine-side candidate selection behaviour and for resource pins: https://proj.org/en/stable/operations/operations_computation.html
National geodetic authority frame and deformation model publications, for example the NOAA National Geodetic Survey modernised reference frames: https://www.ngs.noaa.gov/datums/newdatums/index.shtml

canonicalization_rules: Axis order is canonical as declared by the CRS definition, not as implied by any serialization. Where a binding fixes a different order, the export records that reordering as a declared loss and never rewrites the source declaration.
A CRS reference is canonical as the triple of issuing authority, code and registry release. A bare code without an authority and release is not canonical and must be resolved before use.
An absent CRS field and an explicitly undefined CRS value are distinct and must never be canonicalised to one another; neither is canonicalised to a default CRS.
Coordinate epoch is canonical as a decimal year and is never canonicalised into or out of an RFC 3339 instant, because it denotes a geodetic reference time rather than a record event.
Coordinate values are canonical at their declared precision with their declared axis units; trailing-digit normalisation that changes the declared precision is a value change, not a canonicalisation.
Ring closure and ring orientation are canonicalised only when the target binding declares a required convention, and the applied convention is recorded with the export.
patch_rules: Originals are immutable. Every correction is a new context version that names the version it supersedes, the reason code, the responsible agent and the effective interval.
A patch must state whether it changes coordinate values, the coordinate reference context, or both. A change to either forces a new version regardless of magnitude.

A patch may never change a CRS reference without an accepted transformation evidence record linking the prior and new coordinate values, or an explicit declaration that the prior assignment was erroneous and no transformation was applied.
Any change to a pinned operation, engine version, registry release or resource digest requires a new pin set; pin sets are never edited in place.
A patch must report the impacted reference set. Re-pointing and re-derivation are executed by the owners of the dependents, not by this model.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional coordinate reference context field, an additional loss class or an additional validation check is backward compatible.

Changing a default CRS, an axis order convention, an epoch interpretation, a comparability precondition or the meaning of a failure code is a breaking change and requires a new major version of the adopted package.
Removing a loss class from an export report, or widening a blocking loss threshold, is breaking because downstream consumers relied on the prior guarantee.
A registry release upgrade that deprecates a referenced code is breaking for every binding that references it; the affected bindings must be enumerated before the upgrade is adopted.

Alignment with an external standard is asserted at a named version only. A new version of that standard does not automatically extend the alignment and conformance is never claimed without test evidence.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the artifact: the code issued by the authoritative geodetic registry for a CRS, reference frame or coordinate operation; the host system's own binding key for a binding; the executing engine's own run identifier for a transformation evidence record.

Governed global identifier or IRI issued under a registered naming authority, such as an OGC definition http URI or a registered URN, used when no master-system identifier exists but the resource is published for reuse.

UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only when neither of the preceding tiers applies. A date, a coordinate epoch, a file name, a geometry hash or a bounding box is never an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record every instant as an RFC 3339 date-time with explicit seconds and an explicit numeric UTC offset or Z; never rely on an implied local zone, and use -00:00 only to signal that the local offset is genuinely unknown. Record event time, meaning the instant at which the described spatial fact held, separately from observation or ingestion time, meaning the instant at which the record was captured, returned or loaded, whenever the two differ; an as-of read must state which of the two it was resolved against. Keep both strictly distinct from coordinate epoch, which is a geodetic reference time expressed as a decimal year and is neither an event timestamp nor an observation timestamp.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serially issued artifacts, namely validation reports, transformation evidence records, export loss reports and resolved context snapshots, are named as artifact-kind, binding identifier and a zero-padded monotonically increasing sequence number scoped to that binding. The sequence never encodes a date, a coordinate epoch or a version number, is never reset, and is never reused after a tombstone is issued for the binding.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every issued artifact carries a content digest computed over its canonical form together with the digests of every pinned external resource it depends on, including grid and deformation model files and the registry release. A consumer must reject an artifact whose own digest fails to re-verify, whose pinned registry release is unavailable, or whose resource digests do not match those recorded in the pin set. A newer resource is never substituted silently for a pinned one; substitution requires a new pin set and a new evidence record.

policies: No coordinate value is published, compared or exported without a resolvable coordinate reference system reference; where the referenced frame is dynamic, a coordinate epoch is additionally mandatory. An unresolvable reference produces an explicit failure, never a default.

This model calculates, validates and reports only. Persistence, authorization enforcement, registry curation, grid and deformation resource acquisition, cartographic rendering and physical destruction are performed by the external systems named in the composition links, and no function here asserts control over them.

A derived coordinate value is publishable only with an accepted transformation evidence record that pins operation, engine version, registry release and resource digests. A result produced without a required resource, or by a synthetic ballpark path, must be labelled as degraded and must not be presented as carrying registry accuracy.
Originals are immutable. Every correction is a new version that supersedes a prior one and states its reason, and every superseded version remains readable for as long as retention permits.

No serialization, database or interface binding is canonical. A binding's fixed defaults are recorded as export losses, and a round trip through any binding is treated as lossy until a loss report demonstrates otherwise.

read: An as-of read requires an explicit instant and an explicit statement of which time axis it denotes; the response reports the resolved context version, the coordinate epoch and the registry release in force.

A read that cannot resolve a context version or a CRS reference returns an explicit failure code with the nearest earlier and later version references; it never substitutes a default coordinate reference system or a default epoch.
A read served in a CRS other than the declared storage CRS must reference the transformation evidence record for the values returned, and must carry the degraded indicator where one applies.
The authorization reference presented and the external decision reference returned are recorded on the response for correlation by the audit owner; this model performs no authorization evaluation.
A read served at reduced precision under a redaction rule must declare that it is generalised and cite the redaction reference.
create: Creation of a binding requires a resolvable host record reference, a geometry with a declared geometry kind and coordinate dimension, a resolvable CRS reference with an axis declaration, and a coordinate epoch where the referenced frame is dynamic.
A creation request carries an idempotency key; a replay of the same key within the declared window yields the same reported outcome, and the same key with a different payload is an explicit failure.
Creation produces a binding proposal and an admissibility report. Committing the binding to storage is performed by the external persistence system, and this model reports no commit confirmation.
A binding is not created for a CRS code whose status at the pinned registry release is deprecated; a superseded code may be created only with the superseding reference recorded alongside it.
update: Coordinate values and coordinate reference context are updated only by supersession. In-place mutation of an existing version is prohibited without exception.
A mutating request carries an expected version token; a mismatch is a terminal rejection and no automatic merge of geometry or coordinate reference context is ever performed.
A change of CRS reference requires an accepted transformation evidence record, or an explicit declaration that the prior assignment was erroneous and that no transformation was applied.
Every supersession reports the impacted reference set with a re-derivation obligation per dependent; executing that re-pointing belongs to each dependent's owner.
Changes to a pinned operation, engine version, registry release or resource digest produce a new pin set rather than an amendment to an existing one.
delete: This model never destroys data. A delete request produces a tombstone marker that retains only the binding identifier, the invalidation instant recorded with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, any superseded-by reference and the declared residual payload profile; coordinate values are not retained in the residual unless the retention owner directs otherwise.

Retention periods, disposition approval, hold administration and physical destruction are owned and executed by the adopting Dimension's records-retention and legal-hold model, referenced through the retention policy reference. This model only reports disposition readiness and any asserted hold, and reports readiness as false while any hold reference is unresolved.

A tombstone is refused, with an explicit failure code and the blocking list, while an unresolved hold is asserted or while destruction would break an incoming required reference; referential integrity is reported, and its restoration is executed by the owners of the dependents.

Derived artifacts that reference a tombstoned binding, namely validation reports, transformation evidence records and export loss reports, are retained as provenance under the retention rule that governs them, because their retention and disposition are owned by the provenance and audit record model rather than by this model.

Where locational data is subject to a jurisdiction-specific erasure obligation, this model reports the residual payload profile and any required generalisation; the legal determination and its execution belong to the retention and privacy owners of the adopting Dimension.

roles.name: Geodetic reference steward
responsibilities: Approve the CRS allow-list, the pinned registry release and the coordinate epoch policy for the adopting Dimension.
Review each new registry release for deprecations and supersessions affecting existing bindings, and enumerate the affected bindings before adoption.
Approve default pinned operations and acceptance accuracy tolerances, and approve any use of a degraded or ballpark path.

roles.name: Geometry data custodian
responsibilities: Maintain bindings between host records and geometries, including geometry role and storage CRS declarations.
Initiate corrections by supersession with a reason code and supporting evidence, and circulate the impacted reference set to dependent owners.
Report disposition readiness and asserted holds for bindings entering closure.

roles.name: Transformation operator
responsibilities: Execute pinned coordinate operations in the external engine and return complete evidence including engine version, resource digests and execution instants.
Report missing or unavailable resources rather than silently substituting an alternative operation.
Hold no authority over what is pinned; execution is performed strictly against the issued pin set.

roles.name: Binding and interoperability maintainer
responsibilities: Maintain the catalogue of target bindings with their expressive limits and known loss classes.
Keep the blocking loss classes and thresholds current, and validate that loss reports remain accurate as binding versions change.
Verify that no binding profile is treated as canonical within the adopted package.

roles.name: Access, privacy and retention authority
responsibilities: Own authorization decisions, hold assertions, retention schedules and destruction execution outside this model.
Set jurisdiction-specific location-sensitivity classifications and generalisation thresholds that this model applies as redaction references.
Receive and retain the decision, authorization and export references this model emits, as the owner of the audit trail.

access.default_rule: Read of geometry and coordinate reference context is granted at finding scope by default only where the location is not classified as sensitive. Precise coordinates for a subject classified as location-sensitive default to denied and require an explicit authorization reference resolved by the external decision point; this model records the presented reference and the returned decision reference and performs no evaluation of its own.
exceptions: Precision-reduced or generalised view granted where full precision is denied, served with an explicit generalised indicator and the redaction reference that set the threshold.
Break-glass read for an urgent operational need, permitted only with a mandatory reason reference and flagged for review by the external access authority.
Aggregate-only access for protected sites or protected populations, where individual coordinates are withheld and only derived extents are served.
Embargoed access, where a binding is withheld until a stated effective instant recorded with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
Registry-licensing exception, where redistribution of a referenced registry, grid or deformation resource is restricted and only the reference, not the resource content, may be served.
audit_requirements: Every authorization reference presented, every external decision reference returned and every export loss report identifier must be emitted for capture by the external audit model; this model retains no audit trail of its own.
Break-glass reads must emit the reason reference and be flagged for external review, and the flag must survive in any artifact produced from the read.
Every export served at reduced precision must emit the redaction reference and the resulting effective precision so that the recipient's downstream use can be assessed.
Every acceptance or rejection of transformation evidence must emit the pin set reference and the mismatch list, so that a disputed coordinate value can be re-derived independently.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first and resolve Name, Type and the four URLs before attempting any operation; if any of the four does not resolve, stop and report rather than proceeding on assumptions.
Read the Specification URL to obtain the model scope, the out-of-scope list and the boundary notes, so that operations owned by neighbouring models are not attempted here.
Read the Storage type URL to learn which projection is actually in force and which parts of the coordinate reference context that projection cannot carry.
Read the Interface URL to learn as-of read semantics, the precondition envelope and the failure vocabulary, including the prohibition on defaulting a CRS or epoch.
Read the Processes URL to learn supersession, pin set assembly, evidence verification and disposition-readiness procedures before proposing any change.
Only then perform a read, always supplying an explicit as-of instant and time-axis selector, and never assuming a default coordinate reference system, axis order or coordinate epoch.

coverage.claim: This model states the operation semantics required to read, bind, correct, validate, transform, compare, export and retire a geometry together with its coordinate reference context, grounded in the abstract referencing model, an interface standard for CRS by reference, two serialization standards with documented and differing expressive limits, a registry authority statement, an engine's own account of heuristic operation selection, and a provenance vocabulary. It claims alignment with those sources at the named versions and does not claim conformance to any of them; every structural node carries primary support, and where support is only guidance rather than a testable requirement, the node is stated as a declared local precondition with an explicit failure rather than as a conformance claim.

checklist.notes: Binding, context version, pin set, evidence and report identifiers are defined with a three-tier priority whose first tier is the authoritative master-system identifier, and registry codes are always carried with their issuing authority and release. The finding on comparability explicitly rejects equality of CRS codes as sufficient identity of realization where the datum is an ensemble.

Version states, permitted transitions, correction by supersession over immutable originals, change classes that force a new version, and tombstone marking are all defined. Execution of disposition remains with the retention owner, which is stated rather than assumed.

Host binding with role and cardinality, impacted reference sets on supersession, blocking reference lists on tombstone, and pairwise comparability preconditions are all modelled. Relation algebra itself is delegated by an EXTEND link that specialises only the coordinate-reference precondition.

Event time and observation or ingestion time are separated on reads and in the timestamp rule, effective intervals bound versions, and coordinate epoch is kept strictly distinct as a geodetic decimal-year quantity that is never used as a record timestamp or an identifier.

Transformation evidence, supersession records and invalidation assertions are shaped with entity, activity, agent, used, wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom and wasRevisionOf, with a verification function that rejects evidence not matching its pin set. Storage and retention of provenance belong to the aligned provenance model.

Five roles are defined with explicit boundaries, and the transformation operator is stated to hold no authority over what is pinned. Registry curation, enforcement, audit retention, resource acquisition, rendering and destruction are each assigned to a named external owner.

Structural checks per geometry kind, unconditional and conditional context-completeness obligations, axis and unit agreement, area-of-validity containment, and a severity vocabulary are defined. Validation reports the publication decision input without gating publication itself.

A deny-by-default rule for location-sensitive precise coordinates, four declared scopes, five exception classes including registry-licensing restriction, and emission requirements for the external audit owner. No evaluation or enforcement is performed locally.

Delete produces a tombstone with a minimal residual payload and never destroys data; retention periods, hold administration, disposition approval and destruction are executed by the adopting Dimension's retention and legal-hold model, and derived artifacts are retained under the provenance model's rule.

Format and interface neutrality is enforced by treating every binding as a projection with itemised losses. WKT, GeoJSON, GML, columnar and HTTP interface bindings are each aligned at a named version and none is canonical.

Claimed operation accuracy and its source are carried, and unknown accuracy is representable, but no defensible normative rule was found for propagating uncertainty across a concatenated operation chain or for combining operation accuracy with source coordinate uncertainty. This is stated as an open question rather than resolved.

Registry access is subject to terms of use and several national grid and deformation resources are not freely redistributable, which constrains what a pin set may carry. The model records the constraint and requires the Dimension to declare a licensing position, but does not model licence terms themselves.

Redaction references, generalisation thresholds, precision-reduced views and tombstone residual generalisation are modelled, but thresholds and classifications are explicitly set by the adopting Dimension because they diverge by jurisdiction.

No binding is canonical, binding-fixed defaults are recorded as losses rather than adopted as semantics, and the distinction between an absent CRS field and an explicitly undefined CRS value is preserved across canonicalisation.

Engineering, parametric and temporal CRS kinds are classifiable, but the abstract model restricts dynamic reference frames to geodetic and vertical frames, which is documented as insufficient for orbital, free-flight and deformable-body cases. No settled normative treatment exists, so this is recorded as a gap.

Rendering, symbolisation and generalisation for display are owned by a cartographic model. Generalisation appearing here is redaction for privacy, not display simplification, and is deliberately kept distinct.

known_omissions: No uncertainty propagation model across concatenated coordinate operations, and no rule for combining operation accuracy with source coordinate uncertainty.
No treatment of raster or coverage grid geometry, tiling schemes or discrete global grid cell identifiers beyond noting that some serializations can carry them.
No model of geometry simplification, topological cleaning or conflation, which are transformations of shape rather than of reference frame.
No treatment of moving-object or trajectory geometry where position varies continuously with time as a first-class value rather than as a versioned snapshot.
No treatment of measured or linear referencing along a route, which requires a linear reference system distinct from a coordinate reference system.
No model of the licence terms themselves for registry, grid and deformation resources; only the presence of a constraint is recorded.
No enumeration of database-specific spatial type limits beyond the general statement that database bindings are lossy projections.
No rule for reconciling a geometry whose host record and geometry disagree about which real-world thing is being located.
conflicts: A widely used JSON serialization fixes a single geographic CRS with longitude-first ordering and removed its prior CRS member because alternative CRS caused interoperability failures, while an interface standard in the same family provides CRS by reference with a declared storage CRS. An export to that serialization therefore collapses the CRS reference, and the two sources cannot both be satisfied without a recorded loss.

Coordinate epoch has no slot at all in that JSON serialization, is carried at column rather than geometry granularity in the columnar binding, and is expressed through a separate coordinate-metadata construct in well-known text. Round-tripping a dynamic-frame geometry across these bindings loses or coarsens the epoch in different ways.

Axis order conflicts persist between CRS definitions that declare latitude first, the longitude-first convention fixed by interface and JSON bindings, and legacy identifier-only practice in databases. The conflict is real and is handled by declaring the authoritative axis order and recording reordering as a loss.

A commonly cited geographic CRS identifier denotes a datum ensemble rather than a single realization, so equal identifiers do not establish equal realization; the ensemble accuracy bounds admissible comparison precision. Much tooling treats the identifier as exact, which conflicts with the abstract model.

The registry distinguishes superseded records, which remain valid but have a better equivalent, from deprecated records, which are erroneous. Many toolchains collapse both into a single unusable state, which conflicts with the registry's own semantics and can silently discard valid history.

Version 1 of well-known text is deprecated in favour of the current version, and conversion between them is lossy in both directions for datum ensembles, dynamic frames and usage extents. Systems that persist the older form cannot round-trip current semantics.

The abstract model restricts dynamic reference frames to geodetic and vertical frames, while engineering-report evidence shows this is insufficient for orbital and free-flight cases, and recommends a different encoding for coordinate operations than the one most widely deployed.
regional_assumptions: North American reference-frame modernisation replaces a horizontal datum misaligned from the geocentre by roughly two metres and a vertical datum biased and tilted at the metre level, with four plate-fixed frames and a geopotential datum. Adopting Dimensions in that region must expect a re-derivation obligation across existing bindings; the timeline is set by the national authority, not by this model.

Europe, Australasia and Japan use differing conventions for plate-fixed versus globally aligned frames and for whether coordinates are held at a fixed epoch or propagated. Epoch policy is therefore declared per adopting Dimension and per host collection rather than assumed globally.

National grid and deformation model resources differ in availability, versioning cadence and redistribution permission. A pin set that is reproducible in one jurisdiction may be unreproducible in another because the pinned resource cannot be obtained.

Location-privacy obligations and the threshold at which coordinates become personal or sensitive vary substantially by jurisdiction. Generalisation radii and sensitivity classifications must be set by the adopting Dimension against local law.

Access to the principal geodetic registry requires acceptance of terms of use, which some organisations and jurisdictions treat as a procurement or compliance precondition. The model records this as a licensing hold rather than assuming open access.
adversarial_checks: Tested whether a rule such as assume the geographic CRS when none is stated could be justified model-wide. Rejected: that fixing is normative only inside a specific JSON serialization and inside one interface standard's core, both of which are bindings. Generalising a binding-scoped default into model semantics would be unsupported, so an explicit resolution failure is required instead.

Tested whether this model should own transformation execution. Rejected: the engine's own documentation shows candidate operations are ranked by roughly a dozen criteria including local grid availability and engine version, and that the first-ranked operation is not necessarily the one applied to a given coordinate. Owning execution would embed one implementation's heuristics as semantics, so the model pins, verifies and reports instead.

Tested whether an audit trail belongs in this model, since operations produce decision and authorization references. Rejected: the model emits those references for capture and retains none; the request-precondition finding was deliberately made inline-only and artifact-free so that no competing durable operation record is created here.

Tested whether coordinate epoch could serve as the record timestamp and remove the need for a separate time axis. Rejected: epoch is a geodetic reference time in decimal years attached to the coordinates, not to the record, and the timestamp rule keeps event time, observation time and epoch mutually distinct.

Searched for a normative, testable requirement that spatial relations must be computed in a common CRS. Found the influence of reference systems on geometric computation treated as a first-class concern and relation families defined, but not a universal machine-checkable rule. The comparability gate is therefore stated as a declared local precondition with an explicit failure, not as a conformance claim.

Tested whether identical CRS codes are sufficient evidence that two geometries are comparable. Rejected: where the referenced datum is an ensemble, the ensemble accuracy bounds internal ambiguity, so code equality was demoted to a necessary but not sufficient condition and the ensemble indicator was made a first-class element.

Tested whether a loss report could be reduced to a single lossy flag. Rejected: the sources document distinct and independently consequential loss classes, including CRS collapse, epoch loss, curve linearisation, topology loss and antimeridian splitting, each with a different magnitude and reversibility, so itemisation with magnitude is required.

Tested whether the model could own deletion given that it defines a tombstone. Rejected: the tombstone is an invalidation assertion only; retention periods, hold administration, disposition approval and destruction were moved to a referenced retention model, and readiness is reported as false while any hold is unresolved.
